The water–MDEAH⁺ interaction fits the retained aqueous MDEA/HCl osmotic
coefficients, but its transferred value strongly underpredicts the withheld
MDEA/CO₂ bubble pressures. This calibration-to-prediction failure is a
model-reading and parameter-transfer limit, not a successful absorption prediction.
It does not demonstrate failure of every MDEA model and is not an MEA result.

**Claim class:** osmotic calibration followed by failed held-out pressure
prediction. Numerical solution closure and admitted reference states are
separate from physical agreement.

## Question, conventions and data roles

Can the interaction calibrated to Wangler Tables 8–9/Figure 10 reproduce the
Table 10 pressures without adjusting to them? The osmotic observations are
calibration data in both the source determination and this native fit. The
pressure observations are withheld from those fitted interaction coordinates.
Repeated lanes and allowance probes reuse the same observations.

{{< include figures/notebook-domain.md >}}

The [README](README.md#conventions-330-research-comment-6037145321) records the
source interpretation: multi-segment MDEAH⁺, the Held packing and Debye–Hückel
diameter conventions, fixed printed cross-association values, and water
permittivity for the osmotic fit. S0 excludes ion self-dispersion and is the
primary interpretation; S1 retains it as a diagnostic alternative.
The native fit minimizes Wangler's relative osmotic-coefficient objective
per isotherm using exact Jacobians. Linear interpolation transfers the fitted
interaction to the pressure temperature. This is a declared interpolation,
not an independently established temperature law.

{{< include figures/notebook-metrics.md >}}

The pressure declaration retains Table 2 constants on the unconverted
mole-fraction basis, water at its pure-liquid reference and every other species
at infinite dilution in water, the fixed concentrated-blend permittivity and
a CO₂-rich second-phase start. `figures/figure-14/output/wangler-2018-table-10-native-summary.json:declaration`
owns those conventions and source locators.

## Withheld pressure failure

![Wangler Table 10 pressure observations and discrete predictions after osmotic calibration. Error bars are source standard pressure uncertainties. The printed-interaction lane is a separate diagnostic. The log pressure axis exposes both underprediction and overprediction.](figures/notebook-comparison.png)

{{< include figures/notebook-pressure.md >}}

The pressure rows solve with small retained reaction affinities, but the
fitted lanes miss the physical pressure comparison by far more than the
interaction-allowance probes move the predictions. Numerical closure cannot
turn this miss into physical validation. The printed-interaction lane strongly
overpredicts and uses a different declared seed. The per-row interactions that
would match pressure are diagnostic fits to the withheld observations and are
never substituted into the prediction lanes.

## Transfer diagnosis, uncertainty and limits

The retained osmotic fit shows model discrepancy in the concentration trend.
Its measurement-propagated interaction allowance is not the same quantity as
residual-scaled covariance and does not include model-reading uncertainty.
Source-allowed, source-contradicted and unsourced transfer probes must remain
distinct; the README's transfer diagnosis reports that the examined alternatives
did not close the pressure gap. The inferred difference in the water–MDEAH⁺
cavity/attraction balance remains unresolved. A missing published fitted
temperature dependence or implementation difference is a possible explanation,
not a reproduced fact. No new parameter was tuned to Table 10 for this notebook.

The numerical summaries and row files under `figures/figure-10/output/` and
`figures/figure-14/output/` identify the native wheel. Earlier batch-5 and
`grepe` outputs retain superseded conventions and do not enter the tables or
figure above. No source code parity, loaded-density validation, global stability
or general process-prediction claim follows.
